welcome.title: Let's set up your assistant
welcome.lede: It listens, talks back and gets real work done on this computer. A few short steps, about two minutes.
welcome.fact_commands: It runs commands, opens apps and changes files for you.
welcome.fact_screen: It can see your screen and act on it when you ask.
welcome.fact_cloud: What you say goes to the AI provider you choose.
welcome.fact_costs: Usage is billed by that provider, on your account.
welcome.fact_mistakes: It can make mistakes, including ones that are hard to undo.
welcome.accept: I understand this and use it at my own risk.
welcome.read_terms: Read the full Terms of Use
welcome.accept_failed: Your agreement could not be saved. Check that the app is running, then try again.
welcome.declined_body: You declined, so nothing was set up and nothing was saved. Start the app again anytime and it will ask again.

brain.title: Give it a brain
brain.lede: Your assistant thinks and talks through an AI provider. One API key is enough to start.
brain.local_found: Run on this computer · Ollama found
brain.load_failed: The provider list could not be loaded. You can add a key later under Settings → API Keys.
brain.local_title: Run fully on this computer with Ollama
brain.local_ready: Ollama is running here. Your assistant can think without any cloud account.
brain.local_empty: Ollama is running but has no model yet. Pull one first, for example: ollama pull qwen3.5
brain.local_missing: Install Ollama and your assistant runs fully on this computer, with no account and no key.
brain.local_active: Done. The local model answers from this computer.
brain.applied: Connected. Live voice and thinking now run on {plan}.
brain.partial: Mostly connected. These parts did not switch: {parts}. You can fix them later under Settings → API Keys.
brain.security: Keys go into your system's keychain and only ever to the provider you picked, never into a chat.
brain.gap_none: No API key yet. Chat and voice stay off until you add one under Settings → API Keys.
brain.gap_partial: Some parts did not switch ({parts}). Check them under Settings → API Keys.

plans.openai_live_summary: Live voice and thinking on one OpenAI key.
plans.gemini_live_summary: Live voice and thinking on one Gemini key.

agents.title: Hand off the big jobs
agents.lede: For longer tasks your assistant can pass work to a coding agent you already use. Here is what this computer has.
agents.subscriptions_hint: Sign in with a plan you already have
agents.unavailable: No agent providers are available right now.
agents.ready: {agent} is connected and takes the big jobs.
agents.optional: Optional. Without an agent your assistant still talks, answers and uses its tools.
agents.api_key_hint: Prefer an API key? Add one anytime under Settings → API Keys.
agents.gap: No coding agent yet. Bigger background jobs stay off until you connect one under Settings → API Keys.

permissions.title: Allow access on this Mac
permissions.lede: macOS asks for each ability on its own. Grant them and come back; the list updates itself.
permissions.privacy: Each permission is only used by the feature that needs it. The final restart applies them all.
permissions.gap: Some macOS permissions are missing. Voice, screen and keyboard features stay off until you allow them under Settings → Permissions.

voice.title: How do you call it?
voice.lede: Say a word of your own, or press a shortcut. The word also becomes its name.
voice.wake_body: Say "Hey …" anytime. It listens for your word on this computer.
voice.shortcut_body: Press the Call shortcut to talk. Nothing listens until you do.
voice.name_hint: Pick any word with at least two letters.
voice.trademark: Choose a word that isn't someone else's trademark.
voice.refs_caveat: These links are for information only and may be incomplete.
voice.ack: I'm responsible for the word I choose.
voice.mic_failed: The microphone check did not answer. You can try again later in Settings.
voice.mic_permission: The app may not use the microphone yet. Allow it in your system settings, then test again.
voice.mic_no_device: No microphone found. You can still type, and connect one later.
voice.mic_quiet: Very quiet. Move closer or raise the input volume, then test again.
voice.mic_good: Sounds good. Your voice came through clearly.
voice.skip_after_error: Skip this step and set it up later in Settings
voice.continue_anyway: Continue with the shortcut for now
voice.gap_not_persisted: The choice could not be written to the settings file, so it is gone after the restart. Set it again under Settings → Wake word.
voice.gap_degraded: "{phrase}" is saved, but nothing can hear it yet. Install local speech under Settings → Wake word; the Call shortcut works meanwhile.
voice.gap_skipped: No activation set. Use the Call shortcut, or pick a wake word under Settings.

ready.title: All set
ready.lede: Here is what you set up. One restart applies everything, then a short tour shows you around.
ready.skipped_brain: No API key yet. Chat and voice stay off until you add one under Settings → API Keys.
ready.skipped_agents: No coding agent yet. Connect one anytime under Settings → API Keys.
ready.skipped_permissions: macOS permissions were skipped. Allow them under Settings → Permissions.
ready.skipped_voice: No activation set. Use the Call shortcut, or pick a wake word under Settings.
ready.autostart_hint: Runs quietly in the background after you sign in.
ready.restart_note: The app restarts once and takes about ten seconds to warm up. That's normal.
ready.start_failed: Setup could not be finished. Check that the app is running, then try again.

app_tour.label: App tour
app_tour.replay_body: A short walk through the app with the spotlight, the same one you saw after setup.

steps.voice: This is how you talk to {name}. Click the bar, say your wake word or press your Call keys, then just speak. The wave shows who is talking.
steps.new_chat: Rather type? Start a new chat here, as text or voice. Every conversation lands under Recent chats.
steps.agents: Agents are your team: helpers that take on bigger jobs in the background. Let's look inside.
steps.agents_world: This is the Verse, your agents at work. Click one to chat with it or hand it a job. Next brings you back.
steps.voice_hub: Voice holds dictation into any app, your own word list and spoken shortcuts.
steps.artifacts: Everything {name} makes, from pages to images to reports, is kept in Artifacts.
steps.ide: The Agentic IDE runs coding agents side by side in real terminals, on your own projects.
steps.plugins: Plugins, skills and MCP connect {name} to your apps. The store icon at the bottom opens the Marketplace.
steps.settings: Settings, API keys, costs and your profile live here. You can replay this tour anytime from Settings → App.
steps.done: That's the tour. You're ready: talk to {name} whenever you like.
